questions.question: In which year was the Special Marriage Act passed in India?
questions.solution:
The Special Marriage Act was passed in 1954.
  • Significance: It provides a civil form of marriage for residents of India and all Indian nationals in foreign countries, regardless of the religion or faith followed by either party.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian constitution specifies equality before the law?
questions.solution:
Article 14 specifies Equality before the Law and Equal Protection of the Laws within the territory of India.
  • Concept: No person is above the law, and the state shall not deny any person equality before the law.

questions.question: The Seventy-First Amendment to the Indian Constitution included Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali languages in the _____ Schedule.
questions.solution:
The 71st Amendment Act (1992) included Konkani, Manipuri, and Nepali in the Eighth Schedule.
  • Evolution: The Eighth Schedule originally had 14 languages; after this amendment and the 92nd Amendment, it now contains 22 languages.

questions.question: Directive Principles of State Policy of the Indian constitution are borrowed from the constitution of which country?
questions.solution:
Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) are borrowed from the Irish Constitution (Ireland).
  • Note: Ireland itself borrowed this concept from the Spanish Constitution.

questions.question: Which of the following is related to the concurrent list of the seventh schedule of the Indian constitution?
questions.option_1: Taxes on income other than agricultural income.
questions.solution:
Factories is a subject mentioned in the Concurrent List (List III) of the Seventh Schedule.
  • Union List: Taxes on income other than agriculture.
  • State List: Taxes on agricultural income and Tolls.

questions.question: In which year was the Citizenship Act passed in India?
questions.solution:
The Citizenship Act was passed in 1955.
  • Article 11: It was enacted by Parliament using the power granted under Article 11 to regulate the right of citizenship after the commencement of the Constitution.

questions.question: ______ is an Act of the Parliament of the United Kingdom that partitioned British India into two new independent dominions of India and Pakistan in 1947.
questions.solution:
The Indian Independence Act, 1947 was the UK Parliament act that partitioned British India.
  • Date: It received Royal Assent on July 18, 1947, and created two independent dominions: India and Pakistan.

questions.question: The Eighty-ninth Amendment Act, 2003 of the Indian Constitution established which of the following Commission?
questions.solution:
The 89th Amendment Act (2003) bifurcated the combined commission to establish the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes (Article 338A).
  • Article 338: Deals with the National Commission for Scheduled Castes.

questions.question: Original jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of India is defined under which article of the Indian constitution?
questions.solution:
Article 131 defines the Original Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court.
  • Scope: It allows the SC to hear disputes between the Centre and States, or between two or more States, directly.

questions.question: Part V chapter II of the Indian constitution does not include which of the following provisions?
questions.option_1: Joint sitting of both house of Parliament in certain cases
questions.option_3: Power of President to promulgate Ordinances during recess of Parliament
questions.option_4: Language to be used in Parliament
questions.solution:
Part V, Chapter II covers the Parliament. The power of the President to promulgate Ordinances is under Chapter III (Article 123), hence it is excluded from Chapter II.
  • Chapter II (Arts 79-122): Includes constitution of Parliament, joint sittings, and language.

questions.question: The Article 371A deals with the special provision with respect to which of the following states?
questions.solution:
Article 371A provides special provisions for the state of Nagaland.
  • Special Rights: It protects Naga religious/social practices, customary laws, and ownership of land and resources from Acts of Parliament unless the State Assembly agrees.

questions.question: Which among the following constitutional amendments of the Indian Constitution deals with the formation of Sikkim as a state?
questions.solution:
The 36th Amendment Act (1975) made Sikkim a full-fledged state of the Indian Union.
  • 35th Amendment: Previously made Sikkim an 'Associate State'.

questions.question: Which of the following do/does NOT come under state list of 7th schedule of the Indian constitution?
questions.option_1: Relief of the disabled and unemployable
questions.option_2: Pilgrimages, other than pilgrimages to places outside India
questions.option_3: Regulation of labour and safety in mines and oilfields
questions.option_4: Burials and burial grounds; cremations and cremation grounds
questions.solution:
Regulation of labour and safety in mines and oilfields is a Union List subject.
  • State List: Includes Relief of the disabled, local pilgrimages, and burial/cremation grounds.

questions.question: Article 243K of the Indian constitution is related with which of the following?
questions.option_4: Grounds of disqualification from membership of Panchayat.
questions.solution:
Article 243K specifically deals with the Elections to the Panchayats.
  • State Election Commission: It provides for a State Election Commission to conduct these polls independently.

questions.question: Which Article of the Indian constitution states that “The Council of States shall, as soon as may be, choose a member of the Council to be Deputy Chairman thereof and, so often as the office of Deputy Chairman becomes vacant, the Council shall choose another member to be Deputy Chairman thereof.”?
questions.solution:
Article 89 specifies that the Vice-President is the ex-officio Chairman of the Rajya Sabha and details the appointment of the Deputy Chairman.
  • Choice: It mandates that the Council shall choose a member from amongst themselves to be the Deputy Chairman.

questions.question: Which among the following articles of the Indian constitution deals with the right to equality of opportunity in the matters of public employment?
questions.solution:
Article 16 guarantees equality of opportunity in matters of public employment.
  • Article 17: Abolition of untouchability.
  • Article 18: Abolition of titles.

questions.question: Article 143 of the Indian constitution is related with which of the following?
questions.option_1: Power of the President to consult the Supreme Court
questions.option_2: Power of the President to transfer certain cases from High Courts to Supreme Court
questions.option_3: Power of the President to enlarge jurisdiction of the Supreme Court
questions.option_4: Power of the President to appoint National Judicial Appointments Commission
questions.solution:
Article 143 relates to the Advisory Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court, allowing the President to consult it.
  • Procedure: The President can seek the SC's opinion on questions of law or fact of public importance.

questions.question: Article 72 of the Indian constitution is related with the power of the ______ to grant pardons, etc. and to suspend, remit or commute sentences in certain cases.
questions.solution:
Article 72 grants the President the power to pardon, reprieve, respite, or remit punishment.
  • Court Martial: This power extends to all cases where the punishment is by a Court Martial, unlike the Governor's pardoning power.

questions.question: Article 76 of the Indian constitution is related with the office of which of the following?
questions.solution:
Article 76 provides for the Attorney General of India.
  • Qualifications: The person must be qualified to be appointed as a Judge of the Supreme Court.

questions.question: The First Amendment Act, 1951 of the Indian constitution added which of the following schedules?
questions.solution:
The First Amendment Act (1951) added the Ninth Schedule.
  • Purpose: To protect land reform and other laws included in it from judicial review on the ground of violation of Fundamental Rights.

questions.question: Article 350A of the Indian constitution is related with ______.
questions.option_1: Facilities for instruction in mother-tongue at primary stage
questions.option_2: Language to be used in Supreme Court and High Courts of India
questions.option_3: Direction for development of the Hindi language
questions.solution:
Article 350A directs every state to provide adequate facilities for instruction in the mother-tongue at the primary stage of education.
  • Target: Primarily aimed at children belonging to linguistic minority groups.

questions.question: Which article of the Indian constitution is related with the special provision with respect to the States of Maharashtra and Gujarat?
questions.solution:
Article 371 contains special provisions for Maharashtra and Gujarat regarding the establishment of development boards.
  • Specific Regions: Vidarbha, Marathwada, Saurashtra, and Kutch.

questions.question: Which of the following provision of the Indian constitution is not borrowed from the constitution of Britain?
questions.solution:
Fundamental Rights were NOT borrowed from Britain; they were borrowed from the United States (Bill of Rights).
  • British borrowings: Bicameralism, Rule of Law, and Legislative procedure.
